data.title: Axon (AXON) Stock Price Sinks As Q3 Results Stoke Skydio Doubts
data.description:
Axon Enterprise just took a hit. The stock closed at US$382.56 before the Q3 2026 report and then sank about 18% to US$313 as investors reacted in a hurry. That is a sharp move for a company that just posted roughly US$909 million in quarterly revenue and adjusted EBITDA of US$236 million.

The short term story is fear. The longer term question is whether this level of selloff makes sense when considering Axon’s growing software and services base and the Skydio drone investment that is intended to shape the next several years.

Love Axon Enterprise's growing software and services story but worried about getting caught in another sharp post earnings drop like this one? Take a look at our screener of sturdier balance sheet names in the same spirit with the list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals stocks (24 results).

Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): US$908.6m vs. US$710.6m (higher year on year)
  • Net Income (Excl. Extra Items, Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): US$57.0m vs. a loss of US$2.2m (returned to profit)
  • Basic EPS (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): US$0.70 vs. a loss of US$0.03 per share (moved back into positive territory)
  • Adjusted EBITDA Margin (Q3 2026): 25.9% on adjusted EBITDA of US$236m and revenue of about US$909m (solid profitability on the current scale)

Ask Charlie what Axon really gains from the Skydio deal.

Axon bullish thesis meets ARR and margin test

The optimistic story hangs on Axon converting interest in AI, drones, and counter drone tools into sticky software contracts.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Axon Enterprise continues turning global demand for public safety, AI driven workflows, and counter-drone solutions into long term, high margin recurring contracts despite cost pressures and political scrutiny."

Q3 shows pieces of that playing out. Software & Services reached US$437m and is approaching half of group sales. ARR hit US$1.8b with 40% growth and 126% net revenue retention. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.9% also held up despite memory cost headwinds.

Axon bear case on costs, dilution and timing

The cautious view focuses on hardware drag, funding risk, and how Axon is financing its bets.

"Newer offerings such as counter drone hardware and related services, along with rising memory costs for cameras, are currently a drag on connected devices margins and are expected to weigh on adjusted EBITDA in the near term. If these pressures persist or intensify, they could limit Axon Enterprise’s ability to translate bookings growth into higher gross margin and earnings."

Q3 margins stayed solid, yet management still flags a 50 bps 2026 headwind and even larger pressure in Q4. Revenue guidance was cut by about US$130m after Dedrone delays, and the US$1.15b zero coupon convert plus US$1.2b Skydio deal highlight real dilution and capital allocation questions.

data.title: Iovance Biotherapeutics (IOVA) Stock Edges Higher After Q3 Earnings Progress
data.description:
Iovance Biotherapeutics just posted Q3 2026 numbers that lit up the income statement while only lightly nudging the share price. The stock closed at US$7.74 before the release and now trades near US$8.04, up about 4% on the day. That move looks modest next to a quarter built around roughly US$121.5m in revenue and a sharply smaller net loss of about US$22.3m. For a commercial stage biotech still investing heavily, the emotional tug of a green price screen may be masking how much the loss line has tightened.

Appreciate Iovance Biotherapeutics’ move toward heavier revenue, but remain wary of the ongoing net loss. Screen for biotechs with stronger cash generation profiles using the list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals stocks (24 results).

Q3 2026 Earnings Summary

  • Total Revenue, Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025: US$121.5m vs. US$67.5m (up about 80%)
  • Net Loss, Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025: US$22.3m loss vs. US$91.3m loss (loss narrowed by about 76%)
  • Basic EPS, Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025: US$0.05 loss per share vs. US$0.25 loss per share (per share loss reduced by about 80%)
  • Gross Margin, Q3 2026: Approximately 60% (record level, with management indicating year-to-date margin around 54%)

Iovance flagged a 59% response subgroup in lung cancer. Ask Charlie which Iovance program could move the stock next.

Iovance bull case: commercial reset backed by delivery

The upbeat claim is that Iovance has moved from proving the science to scaling a real product engine.

"What gives me confidence is that the commercial business appears to be improving. The number of treatment centers continues to increase, more doctors are referring patients, manufacturing has become faster and more efficient, and the company expects strong revenue growth this year."

Q3 shows that optimism tied to execution has some footing. Amtagvi sales passed US$100m in a quarter, authorized treatment centers topped 100, and most lots shipped within 30 days. Revenue guidance of US$410m to US$420m was reaffirmed, with gross margin at about 60% and the loss line sharply narrower.

Skeptics argue that past launch missteps and funding anxiety still hang over Iovance.

"After a disappointing commercial launch in 2025, many investors lost confidence and the share price fell sharply. However, I believe the company today is much stronger than the market gives it credit for."

The latest quarter cuts against the idea that launch problems are persisting. Amtagvi demand supported US$121.5m in total revenue, with Proleukin moving in tandem and more than 1,000 patients treated. Cash of roughly US$382m and guidance that the balance funds operations well into 2029 lessen near term financing pressure, even though the share price is still well below earlier highs and the stock fell 38% over 30 days to 6 November.

A Closer Look At Go Fashion (India)'s Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

For the year to September 2026, Go Fashion (India) had an accrual ratio of -0.19. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ₹1.4b, well over the ₹405.7m it reported in profit. Go Fashion (India)'s year-on-year free cash flow was as flat as two-day-old fizzy drink. However, that's not all there is to consider. The accrual ratio is reflecting the impact of unusual items on statutory profit, at least in part.

It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. Fortive Investment Narrative Recap

To own Fortive, you need to be comfortable with a story built on recurring revenue, disciplined cost control and steady capital deployment across cycles. The recent quarter shows revenue of US$1,107.5 million and net income of US$172.5 million, which supports that narrative rather than reshaping it. In the near term, the key swing factor remains execution on higher margin software, services and healthcare workflows that can influence profitability.

The biggest operational risk still sits in product mix and deal execution. A tilt toward lower margin offerings, or bolt on acquisitions that underperform expectations, could pressure net margins even if revenue holds. The latest numbers do not remove that risk. They provide fresher evidence to judge how management is handling it.

The most relevant update right now is Fortive pairing US$300 million of third quarter share repurchases with ongoing interest in bolt on acquisitions, while keeping a modest dividend policy in place. Management has laid out a clear pecking order for cash, with organic investment, targeted deals, buybacks and a growing dividend all in the mix.

That approach connects directly to the current catalysts. Recurring revenue, AI enabled tools and expanded healthcare exposure need consistent investment, while shareholders watch how much of more than US$1 billion of recent free cash flow ends up back in their hands. The risk is not the framework itself, but execution quality on future transactions and the timing of any additional repurchases.

What The Current Fortive Forecasts Assume

data.title: Physicswallah Limited Recorded A 5.3% Miss On Revenue: Analysts Are Revisiting Their Models
data.description:
It's shaping up to be a tough period for Physicswallah Limited (NSE:PWL), which a week ago released some disappointing quarterly results that could have a notable impact on how the market views the stock. Physicswallah missed analyst forecasts, with revenues of ₹12b and statutory earnings per share (EPS) of ₹0.48, falling short by 5.3% and 4.0% respectively. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. With this in mind, we've gathered the latest statutory forecasts to see what the analysts are expecting for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Physicswallah's ten analysts is for revenues of ₹49.5b in 2027. This reflects a decent 15% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to leap 215% to ₹1.02. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of ₹49.5b and earnings per share (EPS) of ₹1.02 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

Check out our latest analysis for Physicswallah

It will come as no surprise then, to learn that the consensus price target is largely unchanged at ₹148. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. There are some variant perceptions on Physicswallah, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at ₹200 and the most bearish at ₹110 per share. This is a fairly broad spread of estimates, suggesting that analysts are forecasting a wide range of possible outcomes for the business.

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of Physicswallah'shistorical trends, as the 33% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 29% annual growth over the past year. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 21% annually. So it's pretty clear that Physicswallah is forecast to grow substantially faster than its industry.

The Bottom Line

The most obvious conclusion is that there's been no major change in the business' prospects in recent times, with the analysts holding their earnings forecasts steady, in line with previous estimates. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on Physicswallah. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. We have forecasts for Physicswallah going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.
